rulings.challenge_claim: The unit buries the book's primary macro-seam device mid-span at a junction the mark layer independently keys, leaves an in-span ketiv/qere undisclosed, and truncates its own frame splice below the gloss paired with it.
rulings.grounds: Two of the three components verify exactly; the first is over-framed. Ketiv/qere: one note falls inside Jer.37.3-Jer.37.10, at MT 37:4, standing in the bytes as בֵּ֥ית הכליא הַכְּלֽוּא (oshb:Jer.37.4, byte; unpointed written form beside the pointed read form, single-witness apparatus). The unit discloses the parashah layer and the paseq layer for this span and no ketiv/qere anywhere, while the note one span later at MT 38:2 is disclosed in the material covering Jer.38.1-Jer.38.6, so the convention is present and simply not applied. Upheld. Quote/gloss parity: the frame splice ends on the construct אֱלֹהֵ֣י while the verse continues יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.37.7, byte), and the rendering paired with it supplies the of-Israel element, so the English exceeds the Hebrew offered and the declared elohei-yisrael signal is never quoted whole. Upheld. The macro-seam component is refined rather than upheld as framed. Both of its facts hold: the onset at MT 37:6 is a verse-initial וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.37.6, byte), a member of the narrative word-event shape, standing inside the span; and a petuchah is keyed to MT 37:5, the junction immediately before it (single-witness, tier-3 weak, never a driver, absence never counterevidence). But the ruled granularity for this narrative complex keeps an embedded oracle with the frame it answers, and the bytes support the unit's disposal of the rival: MT 37:7 continues כֹּ֤ה תֹֽאמְרוּ֙ אֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה הַשֹּׁלֵ֧חַ אֶתְכֶ֛ם אֵלַ֖י (oshb:Jer.37.7, byte), directing the reply back through the same messengers sent at MT 37:3, so there is no addressee change across the 37:5|37:6 junction. The seam therefore stands. What does not stand is the handling of the mark and the calibration. A mark keyed to a verse keys that verse's closing junction, which is exactly how the same field reads the setumah it keys at MT 37:8 and how the neighbouring units read the marks at MT 37:16, MT 38:6 and MT 38:23; here alone the petuchah is re-described as texture on the content of verse 5, which conceals the corroboration the rival actually carries. And high confidence is not supportable while a verse-initial member of the book's primary macro-seam device sits interior with a tier-3 mark keyed to the junction before it and the rival is answered on content alone. Two further findings on this row, byte-verified and outside the challenge as raised. First, the device-note sentence names three shapes and then says the two never blend: the counted system has three disjoint shapes (sweep: 21 / 11 / 4 verses, no shared verse), so the sentence miscounts the system it invokes, and the exclusivity word carries no adjacent digit, which a tier label can never supply. Second, of the three curly-quoted renderings in this unit two are not byte-identical to the staged verses they cite, and the one keyed to web:Jer.37.6 diverges only in a possessive apostrophe stored as the ASCII character where the staged verse carries the typographic one, in a run containing no nested quotation at all. The standing disposition treating this unit's straight-quote flag as falling on the WEB text's own second-level marks therefore does not reach the divergence that is actually present.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: add the in-span ketiv/qere disclosure for MT 37:4, single-witness, present-but-not-engaged, alongside the paseq disclosure already there; and re-word the never-blend sentence to name three shapes with its own digit-bearing count (21 / 11 / 4 verses, disjoint). boundary_rationale: extend the frame splice through יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל so the Hebrew run covers every element the paired rendering carries, and re-collate the extended run at byte tier; re-word the MT 37:5 petuchah so it keys the junction it closes rather than the content of its own verse, matching the junction wording already used for the MT 37:8 setumah in the same field; and restore the staged apostrophe in the rendering keyed to web:Jer.37.6, and for the rendering keyed to web:Jer.37.3 re-cut to a stretch of the staged verse carrying no nested quotation rather than substituting ASCII marks for the staged ones. confidence: high to medium. strongest_rejected_alternative: state that a verse-initial member of the word-event system stands at 37:6 with a tier-3 mark keyed to the junction before it, and that the unit is nevertheless held whole because the reply is directed back through the same messengers. Tests the cure must pass: no apparatus class present in Jer.37.3-Jer.37.10 left undisclosed; the Hebrew run and its paired rendering cover the same elements, byte-collated; every exclusivity word carries an adjacent digit naming the swept object and unit; every curly-quoted rendering is character-identical to its cited staged verse.

rulings.challenge_claim: The unit's substantive original-language work is byte-correct throughout, but it carries an undisclosed ketiv/qere note inside its own span.
rulings.grounds: The note is real and in span. MT 37:19 opens ואיו וְאַיֵּה֙ (oshb:Jer.37.19, byte; unpointed written form beside the pointed read form, single-witness apparatus), inside Jer.37.17-Jer.37.21, and no ketiv/qere disclosure appears in any field, while the same class is disclosed one span later at MT 38:2. Nothing else in the disclosure set is owed: the setumah keyed to MT 37:17 and the petuchah keyed to MT 37:16 at the front junction are both cited under their own types with the two never conflated (single-witness, tier-3 weak), and no paseq seg falls in the span. The substantive work does verify. אֲדֹנִ֣י (oshb:Jer.37.20, byte) carries hiriq under the nun, against qamats at the divine-title sites, so the courtly reading is byte-correct, it is argued from the pointing rather than the consonants, and the forward reference to the second of the two courtly sites lands on אֲדֹנִ֣י (oshb:Jer.38.9, byte), which carries the same pointing. Low severity is right: the note is not the token any content claim leans on, and the omission is an inconsistency rather than a missing practice. One finding outside the challenge as raised, byte-verified: all three curly-quoted renderings in this unit diverge from the staged verses they cite, and the one keyed to web:Jer.37.21 diverges only in a possessive apostrophe, in a run carrying no nested quotation anywhere. The standing disposition that both straight-quote flags on this unit fall on the WEB text's own second-level marks inside properly wrapped runs is therefore refuted for that run at least: the divergence there is a verbatim-fidelity one, not a delimiter-nesting one, and the two arms need separate cures.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: add the in-span ketiv/qere disclosure for MT 37:19, single-witness, present-but-not-engaged. boundary_rationale: restore the staged apostrophe in the rendering keyed to web:Jer.37.21, whose only divergence is that character; for the renderings keyed to web:Jer.37.17 and web:Jer.37.20, which contain second-level quotation, re-cut each run to a stretch of the staged verse that carries no nested quotation rather than substituting ASCII marks, so the verbatim arm and the delimiter arm are satisfied by one edit. Tests the cure must pass: every apparatus class present in Jer.37.17-Jer.37.21 disclosed; every curly-quoted rendering character-identical to its cited staged verse and carrying no second-level quotation mark in either form.

rulings.challenge_claim: The unit's stated name-disambiguation principle is refuted by the very bytes it splices, and both divine formulas standing in its span are left unquoted with the formula's mouth misassigned.
rulings.grounds: Both limbs verify at the bytes. Name forms: the device-note principle that the bytes disambiguate each figure by full patronymic fails in both directions inside this material. MT 21:1 carries פַּשְׁחוּר֙ בֶּן מַלְכִּיָּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.21.1, byte) and MT 38:1 carries וּפַשְׁח֖וּר בֶּן מַלְכִּיָּ֑ה (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte) - the same name-plus-patronymic pair - so the full patronymic joins those two sites rather than separating them, and the chapter-20 priest the note names instead is not the collision. Conversely the embassy member stands as יְהוּכַ֣ל בֶּן שֶֽׁלֶמְיָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.37.3, byte) against וְיוּכַל֙ בֶּן שֶׁ֣לֶמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte), where both elements differ in form, so full-patronymic matching would split one man. The unit also splices two different spellings of the Malchiah name into one row under one English name with no spelling disclosure: מַלְכִּיָּ֑ה (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte) against מַלְכִּיָּ֣הוּ (oshb:Jer.38.6, byte), the second the only such form of that name in the book (sweep: 1 verse) - the exact site the per-attested-spelling rule targets. Frame ownership: two koh-amar frames stand in span, כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ (oshb:Jer.38.2, byte) and כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.38.3, byte). Neither is quoted, the splice offered beginning after the first; the second goes unmentioned; and the declared koh-amar signal therefore rests on no quoted form. The mouth sentence attached to the splice names Yahweh as the formula's mouth, where MT 38:1 reads אֲשֶׁ֧ר יִרְמְיָ֛הוּ מְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶל כָּל הָעָ֖ם (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte), making these the words Jeremiah was speaking to all the people. One refinement of the framing that does not change the outcome: a clause earlier in the same field does say that what the officials heard is Jeremiah's own proclamation, so the defect is a contradictory mouth attribution in one sentence rather than a wholly unnamed mouth, and the cure is a clause rather than a rebuild. One finding outside the challenge as raised, byte-verified: three paseq segs stand inside Jer.38.1-Jer.38.6, two keyed to MT 38:4 and one to MT 38:6 (single-witness, count-only), and the unit discloses no paseq at all, although the units on either side of it in this material do disclose that layer. The three parashah marks it cites, at MT 38:1, MT 38:2 and MT 38:6, are correct under their own type, and the ketiv/qere at MT 38:2 is correctly disclosed and correctly scoped, the splice ending before the pair.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: replace the full-patronymic sentence with the per-site reading the bytes give - name MT 21:1 as the site the full patronymic joins rather than separates, and disclose the two Malchiah spellings the unit itself splices, מַלְכִּיָּ֑ה at MT 38:1 against מַלְכִּיָּ֣הוּ at MT 38:6, with a digit naming the swept object and unit; add the in-span paseq disclosure for MT 38:4 and MT 38:6, single-witness, count-only, no position claimed. boundary_rationale: quote the koh-amar form at MT 38:2 rather than beginning the splice after it, add the second frame at MT 38:3, and re-word the mouth sentence so the formula's mouth is named as Jeremiah relaying it to all the people. Tests the cure must pass: every name form claimed is quoted at its own site in its attested spelling with the count object named before the digit; every declared speech_formula signal has a quoted form standing behind it; every koh-amar citation names whose mouth carries it; every apparatus class present in Jer.38.1-Jer.38.6 disclosed.

rulings.challenge_claim: The unit narrates the exact token that carries the span's only ketiv/qere note without disclosing the note, against the rule that pmark state is checked before any content claim in a K/Q verse.
rulings.grounds: Verified. The one note inside Jer.38.7-Jer.38.13 stands at MT 38:11 as בְּלוֹיֵ֣ הסחבות סְחָב֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.38.11, byte; unpointed written form beside the pointed read form, single-witness apparatus), and the sentence saying Ebedmelech gathers rags and cords characterises precisely that word; no ketiv/qere disclosure appears in any field. The variant is specific to the verse the prose leans on - the parallel one verse later is plain pointed text, בְּלוֹאֵ֨י הַסְּחָב֤וֹת (oshb:Jer.38.12, byte) - so this is not a class the unit could have treated as absent. Medium severity is right, above the same omission where no content claim touches the token. The rest verifies: אֲדֹנִ֣י (oshb:Jer.38.9, byte) carries hiriq under the nun, the second of the book's two courtly sites against the qamats-pointed divine title, and the unit argues the pointing rather than the consonants; the setumah keyed to MT 38:6 at the front junction and the one keyed to MT 38:13 at the close both match under their own type (single-witness, tier-3 weak). The epithet observation is byte-true - the Cushite title is carried at MT 38:7, MT 38:10 and MT 38:12 while MT 38:11 reads עֶֽבֶד מֶ֨לֶךְ (oshb:Jer.38.11, byte) alone - but that is a per-site naming variation, not a defect, and no remedy attaches to it. Two findings outside the challenge as raised, byte-verified. A paseq seg also stands at MT 38:11 (single-witness, count-only), the same verse as the undisclosed note, and is likewise undisclosed, so the omission is the whole apparatus of that verse rather than one class of it. And the rendering keyed to web:Jer.38.7 diverges from the staged verse at two possessive apostrophes, in a run containing no nested quotation at all, so the standing disposition treating this unit's straight-quote flag as falling on the WEB text's own inner marks does not reach the divergence actually present.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: add the in-span disclosures for MT 38:11 - the ketiv/qere, single-witness, with the written and read forms named, and the paseq seg, single-witness, count-only, no position claimed. boundary_rationale: where the prose characterises the rag-and-cord token, state that the word it characterises is the one the note stands on; restore the staged apostrophes in the rendering keyed to web:Jer.38.7; and for the rendering keyed to web:Jer.38.9, which contains second-level quotation, re-cut to a stretch of the staged verse carrying no nested quotation rather than substituting ASCII marks. Tests the cure must pass: every apparatus class present in Jer.38.7-Jer.38.13 disclosed; no content claim rests on a ketiv/qere token without the note disclosed beside it; every curly-quoted rendering character-identical to its cited staged verse.

rulings.challenge_claim: The divine-title claim at 38:17 has no support in the form the unit quotes, blends distinct count objects, and asserts an in-chapter recurrence the bytes do not contain; a cited K/Q verse is also left undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: All four limbs verify, and the first is worse at the bytes than as raised. The device-note run is צִדְקִיָּ֡הוּ כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֩ (oshb:Jer.38.17, byte). It is called the full title stack, yet it carries no title element at all: the stack stands next in the verse as אֱלֹהֵ֨י צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Jer.38.17, byte). The run is non-parallel to its paired rendering at both ends - it opens on the addressee's name, which the rendering does not carry, and it stops before the three-word title the rendering does carry - so the mandatory engagement on a boundary-relevant title claim rests on a splice containing none of it. The object is blended. The form present is the Elohei-tsevaot Elohei-Yisrael stack (sweep: 3 verses - 35:17, 38:17, 44:7), a different count object from the book's signature stack (sweep: 32 verses), of which 38:17 is not a member: swept from the signature form as it stands at MT 39:16, the 32 verses are returned without 38:17 among them. The recurrence claim is false at the bytes: of the 3 verses carrying the form, exactly 1 falls in chapters 37-38, namely 38:17 itself, so the assertion that the same full stack is used elsewhere in these chapters has no site to point to, and it is made with no digit and no swept object. A tier label on the splice does not stand in for a recurrence check. Ketiv/qere: one note stands at MT 38:16, a verse the unit cites for its mark and characterises as the king's sworn oath, with the pair inside that oath clause, חַי יְהוָ֞ה את אֲשֶׁר֩ (oshb:Jer.38.16, byte; single-witness apparatus); no disclosure appears. High severity is right: this is not a wording matter but a title claim, a count object and a recurrence all unsupported at the bytes, in the field where the unit's one declared speech-formula signal is argued. What holds: the parashah marks keyed to MT 38:13, MT 38:16, MT 38:18 and MT 38:19 all match under their own types with the two types never conflated, and the mouth of the oracle is correctly named as Jeremiah's rather than left to the formula. Two findings outside the challenge as raised. A paseq seg stands at MT 38:20, inside Jer.38.14-Jer.38.20 (single-witness, count-only), undisclosed. And the supporting reading offered elsewhere for this unit - that the fuller stack is correctly distinguished from the shorter form used earlier in this narrative - answers a claim the unit does not make: the unit's sentence asserts that the same full stack recurs in these chapters, and that is the sentence the bytes refute.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: re-cut the splice to begin at the koh-amar word and run through the final element of the title, dropping the addressee's name, so the Hebrew covers exactly what the paired rendering carries, and re-collate the run at byte tier; replace the same-full-stack sentence with the byte-true object and its digit - the Elohei-tsevaot Elohei-Yisrael form, 3 verses book-wide, of which this is the only site in chapters 37-38 - and name it as distinct from the 32-verse signature stack; add the in-span disclosures for the MT 38:16 ketiv/qere, single-witness, present-but-not-engaged, and the MT 38:20 paseq, single-witness, count-only, no position claimed. observed_substrate_signals: correct the declared speech_formula key if it does not name the form actually quoted after the re-cut. boundary_rationale: for the renderings keyed to web:Jer.38.14, web:Jer.38.17 and web:Jer.38.19, which contain second-level quotation stored with ASCII marks, re-cut each to a stretch of the staged verse carrying no nested quotation. Tests the cure must pass: the title stack claimed is quoted whole in the Hebrew run and byte-collated; every count object is named before its digit and never blended with a neighbouring stack; every recurrence claim carries a digit-bearing sweep naming its object and unit; every apparatus class present in Jer.38.14-Jer.38.20 disclosed.

rulings.challenge_claim: The unit's front seam cuts inside one unbroken speech turn, and the showing-formula warrant offered for the cut is contradicted by the bytes and withdrawn by the unit's own device note.
rulings.grounds: The bytes carry it. The last speech introduction before the seam is וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ (oshb:Jer.38.20, byte). MT 38:21 then opens וְאִם מָאֵ֥ן אַתָּ֖ה לָצֵ֑את (oshb:Jer.38.21, byte) - a waw-conditional, with no speech introduction, no addressee change, no narrative frame and no dated notice. The verse runs to nine words entire, so the account is exhaustive: nothing in the pointed text marks a unit onset there. A conditional series straddles the junction: אִם יָצֹ֨א תֵצֵ֜א (oshb:Jer.38.17, byte), then וְאִ֣ם לֹֽא תֵצֵ֗א (oshb:Jer.38.18, byte), then MT 38:21's third protasis on the same exit verb. A byte-true construction straddling a unit's own junction argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed, and no field discloses it. One refinement of the framing that strengthens rather than weakens the finding: MT 38:17-38:18 belong to an earlier turn of the same speaker, interrupted by the king at MT 38:19, while MT 38:21 sits inside the turn opened at MT 38:20 - so the series runs across two of Jeremiah's turns, and the seam itself falls inside one of them, which is the fact that kills the cut. The showing formula does not carry the seam either. הִרְאַ֖נִי stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses - 24:1, 38:21). At 24:1 the formula is the verse's own opening, הִרְאַנִי֮ יְהוָה֒ (oshb:Jer.24.1, byte); at 38:21 it is verse-medial, standing behind the conditional. So the device note's plural reference to the book's formal vision reports overstates a form with one other site, carries no digit, and the same note concedes that the showing is embedded inside an ongoing address rather than standing as a separate report - which withdraws the only warrant offered for the cut. The mark layer offers no corroboration at this junction: marks key MT 38:19 and MT 38:23, not MT 38:20 (single-witness, tier-3 weak; stated as non-corroboration only, since absence is never counterevidence). The lesser point also holds: the poetic-lines characterisation of verse 22 rests on the modern line layout of the English, which is tier-4 and never evidence in either direction, and it carries no tier label. High severity is right: once the warrant is withdrawn, the seam has no surviving tier-1 signal standing in its own onset verse. The unit's closing junction is not in question - the petuchah keyed to MT 38:23 sits at it, no ketiv/qere note or paseq seg falls in Jer.38.21-Jer.38.23, and both pointed splices reach byte tier.
rulings.remedy: Two parts, and the boundary part is a PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption - never author work. Author work: device_notes - replace the vision-report sentence with the byte-true form and its digit, the showing verb standing in 2 verses book-wide, verse-initial at 24:1 and verse-medial at 38:21, and drop the plural reference to the book's formal vision reports; boundary_rationale - disclose the conditional series running at MT 38:17, MT 38:18 and MT 38:21 across the unit's own front junction, and either tier-label the poetic-lines characterisation of verse 22 as modern layout or drop it; boundary_rationale - re-cut the rendering keyed to web:Jer.38.22, which stores the staged second-level and single marks as ASCII, to a stretch of the staged verse carrying no nested quotation. Boundary PROPOSAL for adoption: fold Jer.38.21-Jer.38.23 into Jer.38.14-Jer.38.20 as one unit closing at the mark keyed to MT 38:23. Test any retained seam must pass - the test that killed the original: it must cite a tier-1 signal standing in MT 38:21's own bytes other than the embedded showing clause, and must state why the straddling conditional series and the unbroken speech turn opened at MT 38:20 do not argue continuity against it.

rulings.challenge_claim: Two distinct items on one row: that the device notes name the unit continuing the account by its sequence position alone, without the verse anchor the unit's other cross-references carry; and that the closing splice runs past the English it is paired with, the added clause being a temporal protasis left open across the unit's own closing seam without disclosure.
rulings.grounds: Both items hold and they are distinct defects in different fields, not one defect seen twice. First item, in device_notes: the closing sentence carries the custodial notice forward to the day Jerusalem is taken and identifies the continuing account by position alone. The register rule bars positional references to other units and requires every cross-unit reference to be verse-anchored, and the anchor exists - the verse-initial dated frame opens at 39:1, corroborated by a setumah keyed to that verse (single-witness, tier-3 weak). Low severity for this item on its own. Second item, in boundary_rationale, and the heavier of the two: the closing splice ends וְהָיָ֕ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר נִלְכְּדָ֖ה יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Jer.38.28, byte), while the rendering it is said to match stops at the taking of the city and carries no counterpart for that clause - so the Hebrew exceeds the English, and a real divergence between the two witnesses at the unit's own end verse goes undisclosed. That clause is a temporal protasis with no main clause inside the span: the dated notices at MT 39:1 and MT 39:2 intervene and the narrative main clause follows at וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ (oshb:Jer.39.3, byte). A byte-true construction straddling the unit's own closing junction argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed, and the unit instead reads the verse as a clean custodial close at high confidence. Medium severity, and it governs the combined rating. What holds: this unit's apparatus handling is complete. The petuchahs keyed to MT 38:26 and MT 38:27 and the doubled setumah-plus-petuchah keyed to MT 38:28 are all disclosed under their own types and expressly not conflated, the front junction's petuchah at MT 38:23 likewise, and no ketiv/qere note and no paseq seg falls in Jer.38.24-Jer.38.28, so nothing further is owed there. One finding outside both items, byte-verified: the barred positional construction is not confined to this unit - the neighbouring units in this stretch likewise refer to an adjacent unit by position rather than by verse - so the cure for that item is a sweep of the class across the stretch, not a spot fix on one row.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: replace the positional reference with the verse anchor - name the dated onset at 39:1 and the setumah keyed to it, single-witness, tier-3 weak. boundary_rationale: either re-cut the closing splice to end at יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם so the Hebrew and the paired rendering cover the same ground, or keep the full-verse splice and disclose that the rendering carries no counterpart for the trailing clause; in either case add the cross-seam disclosure that the trailing clause is a temporal protasis whose main clause falls beyond the unit's own closing junction; and restore the staged apostrophe in the rendering keyed to web:Jer.38.24 while re-cutting its second-level quotation to a stretch carrying none. confidence: high to medium, since the disclosed straddling construction now stands against the cut. Carry the positional-reference cure as one sweep across the units of this stretch rather than as a single-row edit. Tests the cure must pass: no field names another unit by position; every Hebrew run and its paired rendering cover the same elements; a byte-true device straddling the unit's own junction is disclosed wherever it stands.

rulings.challenge_claim: The closing-seam warrant misstates the verb forms the bytes give at Jer.39.4, and one declared substrate signal is not observed anywhere in the unit's own span.
rulings.grounds: Both components verify at the bytes; the severity is understated. MT 39:4 has a compound subject - Zedekiah together with וְכֹ֣ל אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.39.4, byte) - and both the flight verb and the exit verb attached to it are plural, וַֽ֠יִּבְרְחוּ and וַיֵּצְא֨וּ (oshb:Jer.39.4, byte); the one singular verb in the verse is וַיֵּצֵ֖א (oshb:Jer.39.4, byte), a verb of going out toward the Arabah, not of fleeing. The rejected alternative's stated ground, that verse 4 turns the account onto the king personally with his own verb of flight, is therefore false at the bytes, and it is a form-class claim made with no pointed splice from that verse anywhere in the unit - the only citation of verse 4 in the row is the English one. The seam itself survives, but on a device the unit never names: the narrative-shift onset וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר (oshb:Jer.39.4, byte). The declared narrative-frame key naming a reign change is not observed in Jer.39.1-Jer.39.3: both dated frames count regnal years to one ongoing reign, לְצִדְקִיָּ֨הוּ (oshb:Jer.39.1, byte) and לְצִדְקִיָּ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.39.2, byte), and nothing in the span reports a change of reign.observed_substrate_signals is a dependent field; a declared key with no in-span instance is a field defect, not a wording preference. Severity is refined from low to medium. Two independent byte-false items stand in the unit - a form-class claim in the very field that carries the seam's rejected alternative, and a declared substrate key with no observed instance - and form-class labels carry the same discipline as digits. Neither reaches the boundary, which is why this stops short of high.
